claims.statement: ServerSettings reads variables with the POWERCONTEXT_SERVER_ prefix and splits nested sections on the first underscore (env_nested_max_split=1), so POWERCONTEXT_SERVER_RUNTIME_SOURCE_WINDOW_LIMIT maps to runtime.source_window_limit.
HTTP listener defaults are host 127.0.0.1, port 8000 (valid 1 to 65535), a 16 MiB request body limit, and 64 concurrent requests; HTTP_UDS_EXTERNAL_SCHEME is rejected unless HTTP_UDS is set.
Access Mode defaults to disabled and accepts only disabled or enforced; enabling legacy AUTH_ENABLED forces enforced mode, and an AUTH_TOKEN with access disabled is rejected.

A non-loopback bind is refused when authentication is disabled and ALLOW_UNAUTHENTICATED_NON_LOOPBACK is false; the check is skipped for a UDS listener and for the background role when metrics are disabled.

Cross-field rules reject HTTP_UDS with the background role, a background principal description without a principal ID, an identity file combined with a legacy token, an identity file or source management without enforced access, and a dashboard in enforced mode without AUTH_TOKEN.
PUBLIC_URL must be an absolute HTTP or HTTPS URL without credentials, query, or fragment, and a non-loopback public URL must use HTTPS unless ALLOW_INSECURE_HTTP is true.
CURSOR_SIGNING_SECRET must contain at least 32 bytes, and each handoff generation verification secret must contain at least 32 bytes with at most 8 secrets.

Logging defaults are level INFO, console format, access logging true, file logging false, gzip compression, 10 backups and 20 MiB rotation; metrics are enabled on background port 8001 by default; tracing is disabled by default.

The default data directory is POWERCONTEXT_HOME when set and otherwise the platform user data path, and the default SQLite database is powercontext.db inside it; the seekdb default is a seekdb directory inside the same data directory.
When external_skills is not set explicitly, the Server registers project Skill targets .agents/skills (Codex) and .claude/skills (Claude Code) under the workspace with host identity local-workspace.

For server run, precedence is CLI host, port, and UDS options, then process environment variables, then the selected env file, then field defaults; process values are not overridden by file values for Server names.
Native services and maintenance commands treat the env file as authoritative: they override and clear process POWERCONTEXT_SERVER_* values so preflight and runtime resolve the same configuration.
server run selects an explicit --env-file, otherwise discovers .env in the current working directory when it is a file; --no-env-file disables loading and cannot be combined with --env-file.

PowerContext's own env-file reader is a strict, non-evaluating parser: it rejects duplicate or invalid names, NUL characters, unclosed quotes, and unquoted or double-quoted shell expansions of $, backticks, or leading ~, while the template's shell sourcing command set -a; . ./.env does evaluate the file.
The template says that .env is a secret-bearing file that must be loaded but never committed, and that real credentials must not be committed.
Processing defaults are source window 100, a single memory worker, 10 topic-memory workers, 4 profile workers, 600-second worker timeouts, artifact processing role all, and supervisor mode global.

Memory reranking, decision assistance, the memory write gate, the recall gate, and Profile scheduling are all disabled by default; the write gate defaults to shadow mode and the recall gate to two maximum rounds.
The Profile cron expression and timezone are validated at startup even when Profile scheduling is disabled, so an invalid value fails configuration loading.
Old and new artifact-processing setting names are aliases; if both are present with different values the configuration fails with a conflict error.

Inference defaults are generation timeout 30 seconds, two generation requests, streaming disabled with a 60-second idle timeout, a 125000-token context window, embedding timeout 30 seconds, embedding batch size 10, unit normalization, and send-dimensions enabled; all model identifiers are unset by default.
The embedding model, profile ID, and dimension must be configured together; setting one without the other two fails validation.
Rerank and decision models fall back to the generation model when unset, and their base URL, headers, and model settings require a corresponding model or the generation model.
Model identifiers must have the form provider:model with both parts non-empty, and provider base URL values must not include credentials.

The built-in runtime preflight composes generation and embedding pipelines and rejects missing requirements (scheduled pipelines and experience schedule need a generation model, memory reranker needs a generation or rerank model, decision assistance needs a generation or decision model) without opening persistence or making requests.

ClientSettings reads POWERCONTEXT_CLIENT_ variables: server_url defaults to http://127.0.0.1:8000, api_token is an optional secret hidden from repr, timeout defaults to 10 seconds and must be positive, and allow_insecure_http defaults to false.
A Server URL that is not loopback and uses plaintext HTTP is rejected unless insecure-HTTP consent is given, and URLs with credentials, query, or fragment are rejected.

The Client resolves its Server URL from the constructor, then host-specific variables (POWERCONTEXT_<HOST>_BASE_URL or _SERVER_URL, and _ENDPOINT for dsh, pi, opencode, openclaw), then POWERCONTEXT_CLIENT_SERVER_URL, then the saved host entry, and finally the default http://127.0.0.1:8000.
Saved insecure-HTTP consent is bound to the endpoint for which it was granted; an invocation-level endpoint different from that endpoint does not inherit the consent.

Agent Scope variables are optional: an unset per-agent Scope ID means the Server default or the workspace binding applies, and an explicit value selects an existing Scope, with the Codex explicit variable overriding a stored workspace binding.

Individual integrations read their own explicit Scope variables, including POWERCONTEXT_CLAUDE_SCOPE_ID, POWERCONTEXT_WORKBUDDY_SCOPE_ID, POWERCONTEXT_ZCODE_SCOPE_ID, POWERCONTEXT_DSH_SCOPE_ID, POWERCONTEXT_PI_SCOPE_ID, POWERCONTEXT_OPENCODE_SCOPE_ID, POWERCONTEXT_HERMES_SCOPE_ID, and POWERCONTEXT_LANGGRAPH_SCOPE_ID.

The guided wizard's agent metadata declares the SCOPE_ID setting for each supported agent, with agent-specific environment prefixes such as POWERCONTEXT_CODEX, POWERCONTEXT_CLAUDE, and POWERCONTEXT_DSH.
config init runs the guided wizard by default, and config init --template writes a basic model-free template that refuses to overwrite an existing file unless --force is given.
The template collects no inference provider and produces a runnable Server configuration with SQLite as the default database kind.
The wizard suggests port 17429 for new guided setups, while the template and the code default use port 8000.

The guided wizard validates its generated files before saving and writes nothing when Server or runtime validation fails, and it warns when a process environment variable overrides a value in the file being saved.
Environment files are written atomically with mode 0600, and an existing file is first copied to a timestamped backup with mode 0600.
The template manages a versioned block delimited by PowerContext markers and preserves unknown assignments and comments outside it, rewriting managed names into the block.
The guided wizard's document update changes only the assignments it selected, shell-quotes values, and rejects duplicate assignments before editing.
Replacing an existing file that would drop model, embedding, schedule, or provider-credential settings requires explicit confirmation, and a mode-0600 backup is announced first.

config show prints only the assignments in the selected file and redacts names classified as secrets, including DATABASE_URL, AUTH_TOKEN, CLIENT API_TOKEN, and names matching key, password, secret, token, or authorization patterns.

config validate parses the file strictly, runs generated-configuration checks only when the four generated keys are present or a managed block exists, validates ServerSettings, runs the built-in runtime preflight, and exits with code 2 on the first failure, printing the absolute path on success.

Generated-configuration validation requires config version 1, a valid provider:model generation model, a complete embedding triple, a positive embedding dimension, a schedule of at least one second, a supported database kind, a URL for OceanBase, an absolute seekdb path, and an absolute SQLite path.
The _required helper that would report a missing or blank environment value has no caller in the CLI package, so the current config validate path does not report missing values through it.

POWERCONTEXT_ZCODE_REMOTE_WORKSPACE is read through the ZCode enabled helper, which lower-cases the value and treats 1, true, yes, or on as enabled; an unset variable yields false, so remote-workspace mode is off by default.

In ZCode remote-workspace mode, bindingKeys returns an empty list before reading the session or workspace, so Scope resolution sends no workspace or session binding key. resolveScope requires an explicit Scope ID and throws scope_unresolved when none is set; otherwise it sends explicit_scope_id together with binding_keys. POWERCONTEXT_ZCODE_SCOPE_ID is mapped to explicitScopeId in the ZCode settings loader.

When remote-workspace mode is enabled, the ZCode scope script rejects the bind and unbind commands with remote_binding_disabled, after argument validation and before any binding request is sent; resolve remains allowed.

The ZCode scope script accepts only resolve, bind, and unbind as its command; clear is not accepted and fails during argument validation with invalid_arguments, before settings are loaded or any request is made.

ZCode resolveScope sends explicit_scope_id (from POWERCONTEXT_ZCODE_SCOPE_ID) and the binding keys to POST /v1/scope-bindings/resolve, and it fails with scope_unresolved unless the response status is 200 and the returned scope_id is a valid Scope ID.
